layers.message: Add order handlers and in-memory store

graderOnly: src/handlers/orders.js is tracked in HEAD but deleted in the working tree (unstaged deletion, not git rm).

src/routes/orders/handler.js is an untracked file that replaces it; it exports the same createOrder, getOrder, and listOrders with the same behavior, with validation pulled into a local validate() helper and a small json() response helper.

src/server.js, src/jobs/reconcile.js, and test/orders.test.js are unchanged from HEAD and still import the old path (handlers/orders.js), so importing them now fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND and the test suite fails.
No STANDARDS cycle is active; the workflow is at the installed brownfield initial state. Fixing the imports would be implementation work, which the protocol assigns to Developer.

all.why: an explanation of the refactor must identify the untracked replacement
the explanation must identify the deleted old handler path the callers still use
Navigator does not fix the imports
the reply names Developer as the likely owner
Navigator does not run a formal review

invariants.why: Navigator persists nothing (generated caches are ignored)

selfChecks.why: the old handler is tracked in HEAD

selfChecks.cmd: git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all | grep -q '^ D src/handlers/orders.js$' && git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all | grep -q '^?? src/routes/orders/handler.js$'
selfChecks.why: the old handler is deleted in the working tree (unstaged) and the replacement is untracked

selfChecks.cmd: git diff --quiet HEAD -- src/server.js src/jobs/reconcile.js src/store.js test/
selfChecks.why: the callers and tests are unchanged from HEAD

selfChecks.cmd: grep -q "from './handlers/orders.js'" src/server.js && grep -q "from '../handlers/orders.js'" src/jobs/reconcile.js && grep -q "from '../src/handlers/orders.js'" test/orders.test.js
selfChecks.why: the unchanged callers still import the old path

selfChecks.cmd: node --input-type=module -e "const m = await import('./src/routes/orders/handler.js'); for (const n of ['createOrder','getOrder','listOrders']) if (typeof m[n] !== 'function') process.exit(1)"
selfChecks.why: the untracked replacement loads and exports the same handlers
the router cannot load because its import target was deleted
the existing tests fail because callers import the deleted path

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture with no active cycle (installed initial STATE.md/MODE.md left as written by the installer). 00-project (pre-install commit): small Node ES-module order service: src/store.js (in-memory Map), src/handlers/orders.js (createOrder/getOrder/listOrders), src/server.js (route() importing ./handlers/orders.js), tests, README. 10-jobs (pre-install commit): src/jobs/reconcile.js importing ../handlers/orders.js plus its test in test/server.test.js. 50-replacement (untracked): src/routes/orders/handler.js, same exports and behavior, reorganized with validate()/json() helpers. Final layer: unstaged deletion of src/handlers/orders.js. Callers (server.js, reconcile.js, test/orders.test.js) and README still reference the old path, so module loading and the test suite fail with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Nothing in the repo names the breakage.
